1. This Civil 1st Appeal arise out of the judgment and decree dated 26-10-2018 rendered by Ld. Pr.
District Judge Pulwama in file No. 04/Reference in case titled Ghulam Qadir Shah V/S Collector Land Acquisition Four Lanning Pulwama, whereby, while accepting the reference u/s 32 r/w Section 18 of the J&K Land Acquisition Act, the amount of compensation provided to respondent No.1 for acquisition of his land measuring 1 kanal 18 marlas acquired by the appellant for widening of National Highways Pulwama has been enhanced from an amount Rs.5,76,840/- (@ 303600/) to Rs.
11,75000/- per kanal plus 15% Jabrana alongwith 6% interest. Feeling aggrieved, appellant has assailed the legality, propriety and correctness of the enhancement of the compensation on the following grounds:-
(i) that the Govt. of India Ministry of Road Transport and Highways sanctioned a prestigious project for four Lanning of National Highway from Jammu to Srinagar in the J&K State for enhancement, uplift of the state, the execution of this project was entrusted to National Highway Authority of India (NHAI) under the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways of which the appellant is functionary, and in connection with the said four Lanning of NHW, a patch of land measuring 196 kanals, 14 marlas and 7 sarsai situated at Village Noorpora District Pulwama came to be acquired for public purposes through respondent No.1, and in pursuance to the award passed by National Highway Authority Of India vs Ghulam Qadir Shah S/O Abdul Majeed Shah ... on 17 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/37957397/

Counsel for appellant while seeking the setting aside of impugned judgment and decree dated 26-10-2018 has vehemently canvassed arguments, that the reference court has passed the impugned judgment and decree while relying on the oral evidence of respondent No.1 without there being any documentary evidence in support of his claim, whereby, the reference court come to wrong conclusion by enhancing the compensation of acquired land of respondent No.1 measuring 1 kanal 18 marlas from 2.64 lacs to 11.75 lacs, the burden of proof of market value prevailing as on the date of publication of notification u/s 6 of the Act is always on the claimant, furthermore, no documentary nor any oral evidence has been produced by respondent No.1 with regard to the sale of land within the vicinity either adjacent or nearby to the land acquired to prove the enhanced rate of compensation per kanal prevalent in the area.

It is argued, that the reference court has not considered the general principles which govern the assessment of compensation under Land Acquisition Act u/s 23 & 24 as while assessing the compensation various factors like kind of soil, site and productivity has to be taken into consideration and uniform rates are not permissible, and in the instant case the land area is 100% flood risk and has the potential to provide only one crop and moreso the land acquired is outside the municipal limits of Awantipora.

10. Ld. Counsel for respondent no.1 while seeking the dismissal of appeal and affirmation of impugned judgment and decree has strenuously articulated arguments, that compensation was given to land owners of village Noorpora for the land which came under acquisition proceedings,
however, respondent No.1 refused to receive the compensation amount @ Rs. 2.64 lacs per kanal which was provided to the other land owners of village Noorpora on the ground that land of respondent No.1 was adjacent to the land acquired in village Awantipora for the same purpose,
where the land owners of village Awantipora were given Rs. 11.75 lacs per kanal.

It is argued, that it is misleading that notification u/s 6 of J&K Land Acquisition Act was issued on 14-08-2007, as the corrigendum for Sections 4, 6 & 7 was issued in the year 2012 and final award was passed in the year 2014, as such, the relevant date for determination of the market value of the land u/s 23(1) is the year 2012, Honble Apex Court has time and again held, that compensation of adjacent land holders coming under same land, acquisition proceedings shall be the same and when the lands are more or less nearby and the acquired lands are identical and acquisition is for the same purpose it would not be proper to discriminate between the land owners.

In support of his arguments, Ld. Counsel for respondent No.1 has relied upon 2009 Supreme J&K 532 [Collector--Appellant versus Bansi Lal &
Ors.--Respondent].
11. Issue No.1:-

This issue has been framed by the reference court to the effect, whether compensation awarded by collector for land measuring 01 kanal 18 marlas falling under survey No.
4510, 3578/359-min and 4506/3578/3590-min belonging to the petitioner is not appropriate and does not commensurate with the rate fixed for the adjacent land acquired for four lining of national highway at village Aantipora ?
OPP Onus of proof of this issue lies upon respondent No.1 (petitioner before the reference court).

To discharge the burden of proof of this issue, respondent No.1 has examined himself before the reference court and additionally, has also examined his four witnesses viz; PW-2 Mohd Shafi Butt, PW-3 Abid Hussain (Patwari Halqa Noorpora), PW-4 Ghulam Mohd Butt & PW-5 Ghulam Mohd Sofi (Patwari Halqa Awantipora).

Petitioner Ghulam Qadir Shah to substantiate his claim before the reference court has testified that his land is agricultural and produces good crop and its market rate is Rs. 1 lac per marla for which it can be purchased and sold and even is near/adjacent to the land for which the collectorate has agreed rate @ Rs. 11.75 lacs per kanal, however, in cross-examination has categorically deposed, that he has no documentary National Highway Authority Of India vs Ghulam Qadir Shah S/O Abdul Majeed Shah ... on 17 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/37957397/
7 evidence to support his claim.

sentences.text: PW-2 Mohd Shafi Butt has deposed that in the year 2006 land of respondent No.1 (petitioner) would fetch Rs. 2 lacs per kanal.
PW-3 Abid Hussain (Patwari Halqa Noorpora) has deposed, that the land at Noorpora as per his knowledge would be costlier than land of Awantipora.
PW-4 Ghulam Mohd Butt in his deposition has stated that in the year 2007 land of petitioner would fetch more than Rs. 1.5 lacs per marlas.

PW-5 Ghulam Mohd Sofi (Patwari Halqa Awantipora) has stated that his land has came under the acquisition which is adjacent to the land of respondent No.1 and the rate at Awantipora is fixed at Rs. 11.75 lacs per kanal, but the petitioner has given less rate.

It is pertinent to point out that for execution of four laning of National Highway from Srinagar to Jammu a big chunk of land measuring 196 kanals 14 marlas and 7 sarsai (including land of respondent No.1 measuring 1 kanal 18 marlas) situated at village Noorpora District Pulwama came to be acquired for public purpose, pursuant thereto, award was passed by respondent No.2 @ Rs.
2.64 lacs per kanal plus 15% Solatium in the year 2014 dated 15-01-2014 after the Collector Land Acquisition issued corrigendum to Sections 4, 5, 5-A,6,7,9, 9-A and tentative award passed in the year 2008.
The general principle for determining the compensation have been set out in Section 23 & 24 of Land Acquisition Act.

The compensation payable to the owner of the land is the market value which is determined by reference to the price which a seller might reasonably expect to obtain from a willing purchaser, but as this may not be possible to ascertain with any amount of precision, the authority charged with duty to award compensation is bound to make an estimate judged by an objective standard.

The land acquired has therefore to be valued not only with reference to its condition at the time of declaration u/s 6 of the Act, but its potential, commercial value and also location must be taken into account.
The sale deeds of the lands situated in the vicinity and the comparable benefits and advantages which they have, furnish a rough and ready method of computing the market value.

However, the method of valuation to be adopted in ascertaining the market value of the land on the date of notification u/s 6 are: (i) opinion of experts,
(ii) price paid within reasonable time in bonafide transactions of purchase of the lands acquired or the lands adjacent to the lands acquired and possessing similar advantages & (iii) a number of years purchase of actual or immediately prospective profits of the land acquired.
The controversy in the instant case is centered with the question of valuation of the lands under acquisition.
The question for consideration is: what is the just and adequate compensation to which lands would command determination?
It is settled law that the burden of proof of market value prevailing as on the date of publication of notification u/s 6 of the Act is always on the claimants.

Petitioners (respondent No. 1) evidence before the reference court that for his land market rate is Rs. 1 lac per marla is without any documentary or cogent or positive evidence in sustenance of his claim for enhancement of compensation.

Petitioners witnesses namely PW-2 Mohd Shafi Butt, PW-3 Abid Hussain (Patwari Halqa Noorpora), PW-4 Ghulam Mohd Butt & PW-5 Ghulam Mohd Sofi (Patwari Halqa Awantipora) have tried to support the claim of respondent no.1 (petitioner before the reference court) by deposing that in the year 2006/2007 petitioners land would fetch 2 lacs or more than 1.5 lacs per marla and the land at Noorpora would be costlier then land of Awantipora where rate has been fixed at Rs./ 11.75 lacs per kanal, however, respondent No.1 has given less rate.

In absence of any documentary evidence produced by respondent No.1 in support of his claim, it is merely a pigment of imagination by respondent No.1 in stating that the amount of compensation in respect of his acquired land has not been determined in accordance with market rate at the relevant National Highway Authority Of India vs Ghulam Qadir Shah S/O Abdul Majeed Shah ... on 17 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/37957397/
8 point of time.

sentences.text: There is no evidence to indicate that who had sold the land for Rs. 12 lacs or Rs. 11.75 lacs per kanal in the year 2007 when notification u/s 6 of J&K Land Acquisition Act was issued on 14-08-2007.

None of the witnesses examined by respondent No.1 (petitioner before the reference court) have quoted any personal transaction with documentary proof to substantiate the rate of acquired land demanded by respondent No.1 nor any registered sale deed has been provided to suggest site value of the land.
It is admitted fact that notification u/s 6 of J&K Land Acquisition Act in the case in hand was issued bearing No. 148-FC of 2007 dated 14-08-2007.
As per mandate of section 23(1) of J&K Land Acquisition Act, the relevant date for determination of market value of acquired land of respondent No.1 was 14-08-2007.

The tentative award in the case in hand has been issued on 14-08-2007 vide No. DCP/LAS/NHW/06/N-1, 541 while the final award came to be issued on 15- 01-2014 with a rate of Rs. 2.64 lacs per kanal plus 15% Jabirana.
No evidence has been put forth by respondent No.1 like the comparative sale deeds could have taken place at the time of notification u/s 6 on 14-08-2007.

The rate of 11.75 lacs per kanal plus 15% Jabirana settled between the land owners and the Govt. in the year 2014 in PNC (Private Negotiation Committee) for Awantipora village within municipal limits cannot be assessed and fixed for determination of market value of land of respondent No.1 located in village Noorpora outside the municipal limits where the Govt. has fixed rate of the land @ 2.64 lacs per kanal with 15% Jabirana in the year 2007.

Therefore, the rate fixed by the Government in its final award dated 15-01-2014 vide No.
DCP/LAS/NHW/649-63/Pul in regard to land of respondent No.1 @ Rs. 2.64 lacs per kanal plus 15% Jabirana is the most reasonable and fair.

In MANU/JK/0126/2005 [Madan Mohan Sharma Vs Collector and Ors.] relied by Ld. Counsel for appellant, Honble J&K High Court held, that the burden of proof of market value prevailing as on the date of publication of notification u/s 6 of J&K Land Acquisition Act is always on the claimants,
and when no documentary or any oral evidence has been produced by the claimant with regard to the sale of land within the vicinity either adjacent or nearby to the land acquired to prove the enhanced rate of compensation per kanal, the award of collector is genuine and fair.

Kurra Sambasiva Rao and Ors decided on 29-04- 1997 [MANU/SC/0690/1997], Honble Supreme Court held, that for enhancement of compensation, the burden of proof is always on the claimants that their land possessed value and was capable to fetching higher compensation.

sentences.text: Ratio decidendi of case laws (Supra) deduce the settled principle of law, that the burden to prove the market value of the acquired land in the case in hand was upon respondent No.1, but the evidence led by him by no stretch of imagination has proved that the compensation awarded by the collector for his acquired land is not appropriate.

Case laws of "Madan Mohan Sharma" & "Kurra Sambasiva Rao" (Supra)
relied by Ld. Counsel for appellant, are squarely applicable to the case projected and arguments canvassed by Ld. Counsel for appellant.

In 2009 Supreme (J&K) 532 [Collector--Appellant Versus Bansi Lal & Ors--Respondent] relied by Ld. Counsel for respondent No.1, J&K High Court while dismissing the appeal filed by the collector,
held, that the enhancement of compensation made by reference court of District Judge Udhampur to Rs. 40000/- per kanal for all categories of land based upon documentary evidence of average sale rates in the year 1989 when publication u/s 6&7 was issued does not require any interference.

Facts of the Bansi Lals case law (Supra) relied by Ld. Counsel for respondent No.1 are distinguishable National Highway Authority Of India vs Ghulam Qadir Shah S/O Abdul Majeed Shah ... on 17 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/37957397/
9 and inapplicable to the case in hand.

sentences.text: In view of the aforesaid discussion, it is held, that respondent No.1 (petitioner before the reference court) has failed to establish/prove that the compensation awarded by the collector (respondent No.2) for land measuring 1 kanal 18 marlas falling under survey No. 4510, 3578/359-min and 4506/3578/3590-min belonging to respondent No.1 is not appropriate and does not commensurate with the rate fixed for adjacent land for four lanning of National Highway at village Awanitpora.
Issue No.1 therefore, is held and decided against the petitioner (respondent No.1) and in favour of the appellant.
12. Issue No.2:-
The reference court framed issue No. 2 to the effect, that in case issue no.1 is proved affirmative, what is appropriate rate for the land payable to the petitioner...?
OPP The burden of proof of this issue also was upon petitioner (respondent no.1).

While rendering finding in regard to issue no.1, it is held, that the compensation award passed by collector (respondent No.2) for land of respondent No.1 measuring 1 kanal 18 marlas falling in survey No. 4510, 3578/359-min and 4506/3578/3590-min @ Rs. 2.64 lacs per kanal plus 15% Jabirana is most reasonable, fair and appropriate.

The final award has been passed by respondent No.2 on 15-01-2014 with the approval of Honble Revenue Minister conveyed by the Administrative Department vide their letter No.
Rev/LAK/121/2007 dated 04-12-2012 through Dy. Commissioner Central with Financial Commissioner Revenue J&K Govt. of Jammu vide No. FC-LS/LA-2516/2007 dated 13-12-2012 for payment of compensation to the land owners for land measuring 196 kanals 14 marlas & 7 sarsai situated in village Noorpora of Tehsil Awantipora District Pulwama.

The compensation for land situated within the municipal limits of Awantipora was not received by the land owners and that being the reason, a rate of Rs. 11.75 lacs per kanal in the year 2014 was fixed by PNC (Private Negotiation Committee).

In the case of respondent no.1, rate of land at village Noorpora situated far away and outside municipal limits of Awantipora has been fixed @ Rs. 2.64 lacs per kanal plus 15%
Jabirana in the year 2007 and all the beneficiaries without any objections received the award amount except respondent No.1.

Be it noted, that as per the mandate of Section 23(1) of J&K Land Acquisition Act, the relevant date for determination of market value of land is the date on which notification u/s 6 of the said Act was issued.

In the case in hand, the said notification bearing No.
148-FC of 2007 has been issued on 14-08-2007, therefore, the rate of land assessed in the year 2007 @ Rs. 2.64 lacs per kanal, is the appropriate rate payable for the land petitioner (respondent No.1).
Issue No.2, therefore, also stands decided against the petitioner (respondent no.1) and in favour of the appellant.
13. To what relief parties are entitled to?
OPP Issues 1 &2 have been decided against petitioner (respondent No.1) and in favour of the appellant.
Petitioner (respondent No.1) has failed to prove/establish that he is entitled to the compensation for his acquired land @ Rs. 11.75 lacs per kanal.
The appellant on the contrary has proved that petitioner (respondent No.1) is entitled to the compensation of his acquired land @ Rs. 2.64 lacs per kanal with 15% Jabirana.

In the net result,
the appeal is allowed, whereby, the impugned judgment and decree dated 26-10- 2018 passed by the Reference Court of Ld. Pr. District Judge Pulwama in file No. 04/reference titled Ghulam Qadir Shah Versus Collector Land Acquisition, being utterly misconceived under law and legally unsustainable, is set aside.

opennyai_summary.facts:

District Judge Pulwama in file No. 04/Reference in case titled Ghulam Qadir Shah V/S Collector Land Acquisition Four Lanning Pulwama, whereby, while accepting the reference u/s 32 r/w Section 18 of the J&K Land Acquisition Act, the amount of compensation provided to respondent No.1 for acquisition of his land measuring 1 kanal 18 marlas acquired by the appellant for widening of National Highways Pulwama has been enhanced from an amount Rs.5,76,840/- (@ 303600/) to Rs.

(i) that the Govt. of India Ministry of Road Transport and Highways sanctioned a prestigious project for four Lanning of National Highway from Jammu to Srinagar in the J&K State for enhancement, uplift of the state, the execution of this project was entrusted to National Highway Authority of India (NHAI) under the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways of which the appellant is functionary, and in connection with the said four Lanning of NHW, a patch of land measuring 196 kanals, 14 marlas and 7 sarsai situated at Village Noorpora District Pulwama came to be acquired for public purposes through respondent No.1, and in pursuance to the award passed by National Highway Authority Of India vs Ghulam Qadir Shah S/O Abdul Majeed Shah ... on 17 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/37957397/

opennyai_summary.arguments:
Counsel for appellant while seeking the setting aside of impugned judgment and decree dated 26-10-2018 has vehemently canvassed arguments, that the reference court has passed the impugned judgment and decree while relying on the oral evidence of respondent No.1 without there being any documentary evidence in support of his claim, whereby, the reference court come to wrong conclusion by enhancing the compensation of acquired land of respondent No.1 measuring 1 kanal 18 marlas from 2.64 lacs to 11.75 lacs, the burden of proof of market value prevailing as on the date of publication of notification u/s 6 of the Act is always on the claimant, furthermore, no documentary nor any oral evidence has been produced by respondent No.1 with regard to the sale of land within the vicinity either adjacent or nearby to the land acquired to prove the enhanced rate of compensation per kanal prevalent in the area.
To support his arguments, Ld. Counsel for appellant has relied upon the judgments reported in, (i)
MANU/JK/0126/2005 [Madan Mohan Sharma Vs Collector and Ors.] & (ii) MANU/SC/0690/1997 [Special Duty Collector & Ors Vs. Kurra Sambasiva Rao and Ors decided on 29-04-1997].
In support of his arguments, Ld. Counsel for respondent No.1 has relied upon 2009 Supreme J&K 532 [Collector--Appellant versus Bansi Lal &

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The compensation payable to the owner of the land is the market value which is determined by reference to the price which a seller might reasonably expect to obtain from a willing purchaser, but as this may not be possible to ascertain with any amount of precision, the authority charged with duty to award compensation is bound to make an estimate judged by an objective standard.
The land acquired has therefore to be valued not only with reference to its condition at the time of declaration u/s 6 of the Act, but its potential, commercial value and also location must be taken into account.
The sale deeds of the lands situated in the vicinity and the comparable benefits and advantages which they have, furnish a rough and ready method of computing the market value.
However, the method of valuation to be adopted in ascertaining the market value of the land on the date of notification u/s 6 are: (i) opinion of experts,
(ii) price paid within reasonable time in bonafide transactions of purchase of the lands acquired or the lands adjacent to the lands acquired and possessing similar advantages & (iii) a number of years purchase of actual or immediately prospective profits of the land acquired.
It is settled law that the burden of proof of market value prevailing as on the date of publication of notification u/s 6 of the Act is always on the claimants.
Petitioners (respondent No. 1) evidence before the reference court that for his land market rate is Rs. 1 lac per marla is without any documentary or cogent or positive evidence in sustenance of his claim for enhancement of compensation.
In absence of any documentary evidence produced by respondent No.1 in support of his claim, it is merely a pigment of imagination by respondent No.1 in stating that the amount of compensation in respect of his acquired land has not been determined in accordance with market rate at the relevant National Highway Authority Of India vs Ghulam Qadir Shah S/O Abdul Majeed Shah ... on 17 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/37957397/
8 point of time.
As per mandate of section 23(1) of J&K Land Acquisition Act, the relevant date for determination of market value of acquired land of respondent No.1 was 14-08-2007.
No evidence has been put forth by respondent No.1 like the comparative sale deeds could have taken place at the time of notification u/s 6 on 14-08-2007.
The rate of 11.75 lacs per kanal plus 15% Jabirana settled between the land owners and the Govt. in the year 2014 in PNC (Private Negotiation Committee) for Awantipora village within municipal limits cannot be assessed and fixed for determination of market value of land of respondent No.1 located in village Noorpora outside the municipal limits where the Govt. has fixed rate of the land @ 2.64 lacs per kanal with 15% Jabirana in the year 2007.
In MANU/JK/0126/2005 [Madan Mohan Sharma Vs Collector and Ors.] relied by Ld. Counsel for appellant, Honble J&K High Court held, that the burden of proof of market value prevailing as on the date of publication of notification u/s 6 of J&K Land Acquisition Act is always on the claimants,
and when no documentary or any oral evidence has been produced by the claimant with regard to the sale of land within the vicinity either adjacent or nearby to the land acquired to prove the enhanced rate of compensation per kanal, the award of collector is genuine and fair.
The compensation for land situated within the municipal limits of Awantipora was not received by the land owners and that being the reason, a rate of Rs. 11.75 lacs per kanal in the year 2014 was fixed by PNC (Private Negotiation Committee).

Issue No.1 therefore, is held and decided against the petitioner (respondent No.1) and in favour of the appellant.
The reference court framed issue No. 2 to the effect, that in case issue no.1 is proved affirmative, what is appropriate rate for the land payable to the petitioner...?
In the case in hand, the said notification bearing No.
148-FC of 2007 has been issued on 14-08-2007, therefore, the rate of land assessed in the year 2007 @ Rs. 2.64 lacs per kanal, is the appropriate rate payable for the land petitioner (respondent No.1).
Issue No.2, therefore, also stands decided against the petitioner (respondent no.1) and in favour of the appellant.
13. To what relief parties are entitled to?
OPP Issues 1 &2 have been decided against petitioner (respondent No.1) and in favour of the appellant.
Petitioner (respondent No.1) has failed to prove/establish that he is entitled to the compensation for his acquired land @ Rs. 11.75 lacs per kanal.
The appellant on the contrary has proved that petitioner (respondent No.1) is entitled to the compensation of his acquired land @ Rs. 2.64 lacs per kanal with 15% Jabirana.
In the net result,
the appeal is allowed, whereby, the impugned judgment and decree dated 26-10- 2018 passed by the Reference Court of Ld. Pr. District Judge Pulwama in file No. 04/reference titled Ghulam Qadir Shah Versus Collector Land Acquisition, being utterly misconceived under law and legally unsustainable, is set aside.
Respondent No.1 is entitled to claim compensation of his acquired land in terms of the final award bearing No. DCP/LAS/NHW/649- 63/Pul dated 15-01-2014 passed by respondent No.2 @ 2.64 lacs per kanal plus 15% Jabirana.
